A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same procedural-generalization study. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and visually inspected figures, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training experiments, benchmark accuracies, curriculum comparisons, correlation analyses, and qualitative results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds curriculum ablations, SFT/LoRA comparisons, and qualitative error examples.

M1.justification: The proposed symbolic-to-natural-language GRPO curriculum, representation construction, and training objectives remain unchanged. The additional training variants are evaluated as ablations and comparison conditions.

E1.justification: Both versions use asynchronous planning in NL, Graph, and Code, the NL-AAVE variant, MATH levels 4–5, and SciBench physics. The new curriculum experiments and qualitative examples remain within this existing coverage.

E2.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 add targeted curriculum comparisons with interleaved Graph+NL training, standard SFT, and rank-8/16 LoRA, alongside alternative symbolic training mixtures. The original post-training methods, model comparisons, and GPT baselines are retained.

E3.justification: New experimental settings include two- versus four-epoch SFT, a two-plus-two-epoch SFT curriculum, 40-step interleaved training, and Graph-to-Code training compared with 80-step Code-only training. Existing dataset splits, metrics, and main experimental budgets are unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's reversed-order and distillation controls, v2 substantially expands curriculum diagnostics: sequential versus interleaved learning, Graph versus Code or mixed warm-ups, transfer to Code, and SFT/LoRA alternatives. Appendix A.7 also adds another naive-summation example and a residual time-unit error after curriculum training.

E5.justification: McNemar testing, Pearson correlations, and the appendix p-value reporting remain unchanged. Neither version reports repeated training runs or seed-based uncertainty, and v2 introduces no new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 retain their results after matching Table 2's reordered columns. Added ablation outcomes include NL accuracy of 0.382 for interleaved training and 0.533 for Graph+Code-to-NL, plus Code accuracy of 0.787 for Graph-to-Code versus 0.373 for Code-only training. SFT outcomes and qualitative failures are also added; these concern new conditions rather than revised main results.

T1.justification: The DAG formulation, analogical-strength definition, Equation 1, and its implementation formula are unchanged. The added kernel-based perspective is conceptual discussion, without a new formal definition, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The central claims remain: symbolic-only training transfers poorly, the two-stage curriculum improves generalization, and successful transfer is consistent with generative analogy. Calling the curriculum reinforcement learning in the revised abstract and introduction clarifies what v1 already specifies in its method and conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations involving task interference and the importance of a strong first training stage. It clarifies the analogy analysis's scope, discusses moderate correlations and a kernel interpretation, attributes residual errors to base-model limitations, and identifies scaling the number of training representations as an open question.

D1.justification: v2 specifies LoRA ranks and training schedules for the added controls and expands the explanation of budget matching in Section 4.1. Existing appendix hardware, generation settings, prompts, and code/data access destinations are retained; the revised hyperlink wording does not change resource access.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hu et al. (2022) for LoRA and Pentina et al. (2015) and Standley et al. (2020) to connect the new ablations with curriculum learning and task interference. The broader positioning relative to procedural learning and analogical reasoning remains stable.

P1.justification: Changes include localized wording corrections, explanatory footnotes, the new Section 4.2 and subsequent renumbering, updated affiliations and publication information, and removal of Appendix A.10's contribution statement. The overall narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with rearranged panels and a horizontal arrow; Figure 2 gains numerical delta annotations. Table 1 moves, Table 2 reverses its Math/Physics columns, and surrounding content reflows. The appendix plots are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added curriculum controls in Sections 4.1–4.2 strengthen the evidence about when the approach helps, while the clarified analysis and Appendix A.7 failure case make its boundaries clearer. These are useful, focused improvements to an otherwise stable paper. The gain is limited by sparse reporting of the new comparisons, including an incompletely explained equal-budget claim for 40-step interleaved versus 80-step sequential training.
